tips.comment: Jannah Star has been in the frame in all three of her races so far and in two of them she was headed in the final furlong. She looks to have every chance of losing her maiden tag in this 12f fillies maiden.

Ledecky could be right in the 'swim' of things on debut here with the talented Nicola Burns claiming seven pounds and being prepared by a top trainer who knows how to get them ready to fire first-up. Bred to handle softer ground.

The model I run suggests Eternal Spirit can win this one. Eternal Spirit lines up here with the second highest RPR for the 11-runner field but carries the same weight as the majority of the other runners. 10 lbs less initial weight than 4 of the top weights. Eternal Spirit tries the blinkers for the first time in first outing for over 280 days. Race fitness might be a concern and will need to go well fresh. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Looks like the stable's second string for Joseph O'Brien, but Onaqui has claims on form. By Derby winner Camelot. Debut was in April (95 days ago), so entitled to step forward from that. Slowly away that day but stayed on late. Second start for a strong stable.

Jarrive De Mee has been ridden by Patrick Mullins in all four of his hurdle races for Willie Mullins, having previously been a winning pointer. He won his first three hurdle races, none of which had much strength of opposition, before finishing 4th of 8 in a Grade 1 hurdle at Punchestown. If he puts his pointing experience to good use, he may come out on top in this 18-runner beginners' chase, in which his stablemate Uncle Pat is his biggest danger.

3rd on reappearance run last time, his chase debut on first run for 8 months. Jumped well enough and led until lack of recent run told and passed by winner 3 out. Not given hard time and will last longer in this.

SANDOR CLEGANE has jumps experience and has been given time since hurdling when last seen. Top chase jockey Sean O'Keefe steps forward and there is at least a suspicion this low-mileage type has been set aside aimed at this meeting. Decent value angle.

Made a promising chase debut at Tipperary in May when having jumped pretty well he stayed on into 4th over a trip very much on the short side. Connections kept him to that sort of trip next time at Ballinrobe but he failed to give his running and finished a well beaten 4th. Was a never nearer 4th back at Tipperary last time again over an unsuitable trip. Goes up in trip now which should suit and looks to hold decent claims.
Coming off of a break and could be dangerous. Already been clipped in the market, so I see some good each way potential here. Chase debut.

Jack Kennedy has selected this one over Beaufort Scale, who is the top weight. Whats Up Darling was disappointing and might have had an off day at Punchestown. The handicapper has eased him down to 131, and Whats Up Darling could be exploiting this mark in a big way.

A small ew on Millforce who has done quite well over hurdles and was pulled up lto after a short break and was found to have a nasel discharge. Trusting all is now well and horse is fit, will hopefully take to these bigger obsticles and at least get a place.

Donnie Devito is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Ross O'Sullivan and ridden by Donald Meyler. He is twice a winner over hurdles last year, posting an RPR of 125 on good ground and is a course winner. He makes his third start as a chaser and ran better last time out than on his chase debut. Donald Meyler is riding exceptionally well at the moment, finishing 1-3-2-5-2-1 on his last six rides, all at Galway. Donnie Devito may turn the corner now back at Galway on ground which suits and is stepped up to 2m 6f, which should suit as he was doing his best work late on over a shorter trip last time out, having been held up in the rear.

The model I run suggests a huge upset from Justabitofyours. This result has been driven by Justabitofyours having a comparably high RPR to the other runners but the lowest weight to carry around this 2m 6f beginners chase. Justabitofyours has come second in some recent races but will need significant improvement to go close. 200/1 suggests a less than 0.5% implied probability of the horse coming in. My model suggests the chance is closer to 5%, and so this is the value bet. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator. I don't play each way, but clearly, these odds offer the ability to do that if you prefer that betting style.

Acapulco Bay has been in the frame in four of his five runs this season, following on from his promising two-year-old career where he finished 2nd and 1st in his two runs. He disappointed in his only run in a handicap when only 3rd of 6 at Down Royal, but off the same mark of 99, he may be better suited to this big field handicap.

This horse definitely has a bigger performance in him, and it's interesting Willie Mullins has put him in this valuable Galway handicap. He has been well fancied on pretty much all his starts and wasn't asked for any effort last time when he was badly hampered and was just looked after. So he is fresh coming here and looks ready to peak, and I can't miss him today.

Returns to handicap company here after running well @ listed level the last twice. Is only 3lb higher here than Lto run and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Re-opposes Cloud Seeker and has to overcome a potential weight swing, but was staying on the best out of the two that day. Today's softer ground may suit Fleetfoot more. Tends to race prominently, which has been the best tactic at this meeting so far.

Meant to do the other one each way and leave it at that. So, have to take one each way in this field. Plumped with Cloud Seeker, who has strong staying ability, and the ground will be more than suited as well.
This horse went very close last time out with a claimer on board who did very little in the saddle. But with winning course form and a better jockey, I fancy his chances.
En Or is a six-time winner and last time was beaten 4 1/4 lengths at Longchamp when not gaining a clear run until too late. Each way chance.

Ran really well on his return when a close 3rd in a big field handicap over an extended 8f at Limerick. Didn’t get the clearest of runs and did well to finish so close in the end. That came on heavy ground and he was a respectable 7th of 18 at the Curragh next time before a close up 9th at the same track last time up at 12f. Kept to that trip here and from the same mark looks a strong player.
The trainer has got 2 entered in this race as they are putting the first-time hood on this one with a good jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Layfayette is an old favorite of mine as he tends to be in the money a lot without winning. It's worth a shot this returns to handicap, which he has not done for a long time could go well, with his latest run being a G3 second. This does put him a bit heavy, but that is with good cause. It's worth an Each Way with 5P on offer.

It will be interesting how they run Extensio here. Aiming for the big one at York, so this was put in over a mile and was embarrassingly ridden when super restrained last till it jogged past a few. Returns to a more suitable distance with a winning pilot on board, so at least a place here would do it no harm.

Most of my fancies are all drawn really bad and i looked at this one the other day, but was up in trip and didn't get it. Is still 12lb above that last win over this distance back in June, but does have a 5lb claimer today and is drawn well and could well have more to offer.

All runs since coming to Ireland have been jump races and has been pretty avaerage with just one or two good runs. Won last race on the flat when with Julie Camacho a year ago, so maybe a change of code and head gear could do the trick. Small ew for betting.
Won a big field handicap here last time. Runs under a penalty here but is unlikely to stop the winning run from continuing.

EMPRESS ALMA was in double winning form at this time last season and could well be a summer developer. She comes from a powerful dual-purpose Irish yard and she is a race-fit ground-versatile filly. She has an experienced pilot aboard and can be expected to show up well.
Some nice prices in this race as there are a few questions over the favorite. Taking J Martin to have this horse ready after a couple of back-to-back wins. They can make it a hat trick here.
Preparations is one from the tracker from the Slattery yard. It was held up but fared pretty well in the context of the race and so looks a tad overpriced here.
Looks a big price here, and I'm taking it each way with 5 places available. Gordon Elliott trained, and although the ground won't be super beneficial, it can still run a big race here.

Beautiful Chaos has only won one of her 31 starts but placed on 9 occasions, showing she is worth EW consideration. She had been placed in two of her last three starts on the flat last year before switching to hurdles without much success. However, back on the flat at Down Royal, she was second, beaten just a head in an apprentice handicap. Although raised 3 lbs, her apprentice jockey claims that back, and she looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

The model I run suggests an upset from Spanish John. This result has been driven by Spanish John having a comparably high RPR to the other runners but an official ranking which is joint lowest. This subsequently means he steps out carrying the joint lowest weight over the 1m 6f distance. High stall draw isn't helpful, but when the race is bordering on 2m, it should be negligible. Spanish John is currently the third reserve, so might not even run.

Bunting is my choice from what should be a battle between the front two in the market. Bunting is owned by Tony Bloom, a man that likes a punt and doesn't tend to waste his money. This feels like a nice one as there is a lot of deadwood in this race. Another one for Willie Mullins.
Ran okay at Ascot recently but has a nice draw today. The booking of Seamie Heffernan is a plus, and the ground and trip will be no problem today. Nice e/w price.

His trainer, Henry De Bromhead, has a good record in this race, winning four contests and placing numerous times. He's a chaser on looks and was possibly out of his depth in a listed handicap at Punchestown at the end of last season. But if he can get a good position at the front, which he needs, and can put the field under pressure with his good jumping, his mark could be exploited.

As it always seems to be the way here at Galway Gordon Elliot arrives here mob handed with many talented charges amongst his ranks, myself however am siding with his 9 year old Gelding MARS HARPER who is very capable but most importantly knows the time of day here at Galway which a good friend of mine & Fellow tipster ( Sean McNamara: Give him a follow he knows his stuff) so rightly calls it 'A glorified dog track' the horses are constantly turning so Course experience is vital (in my humble opinion). This Son of SULAMANI drops in class here today which speaks volumes of the battles he's been in recently with his run at this year's Cheltenham very impressive outrunning his 100/1 odds to finish 4th. Stable #1 jockey Jack Kennedy picks this charge over the rest to lead him into battle with jockey currently in fine fettle since returning from injury. 16/1 with 5 places is enough for me.
Mother Mara is a useful type who is likely to appreciate the yielding nature of the track here. Gerald O'Leary should have this horse ready to shine here.

Ribee is a solid choice for the win at 6.50. This horse has shown consistent improvement in recent handicaps, traveling strongly and finishing second twice. A return to this distance could be exactly what he needs to break his maiden.

Rizal is a 3yo gelding trained by J P Murtagh and ridden by Ben Coen a formidable team makes handicap debut after a gelding operation - bred by the Aga Khan he is out of a dam that posted a career high RPR of 96 and was a half sister to Rajapour (105) Ridenza (98) whom performed best over todays mile - Murtagh drops Rizal back down to a mile after two attempts over 1m 2f and with some racecourse experience and a gelding operation he should certainly prove to be a better horse than a current mark of 68 and was clearly thought to have some ability when finishing down the field on Gowran Park debut when heavily backed into 7-4f Fein an opening 100-30.

Clever And Classy has been in excellent form recently, winning at Roscommon on 1st July and then finishing second to a well-handicapped rival at Navan two weeks later. She is up 3 lbs and is first reserve, but if she gets a run, she looks like a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.
Elusive Duke at 17.00. He won over a similar trip at Leopardstown and his last run suggests he's still in good form. With a new trainer and a potential pace advantage, he could outperform his odds.

In The Minus has had 20 runs with 1 win and 2 places, a 5% win rate and 15% place rate. Trained by Brian Francis Cawley, he carries 9-7 off a mark of 62. He impressed me with a 3-length win off 52 at Limerick two starts ago and ran respectably when second in a claimer last time. The wide draw in stall 21 is far from ideal, and he is unproven at the trip, but he arrives in fair form and may grab each-way claims at a decent enough price if getting cover and settling early.

The model I run suggests an upset from William F Browne. This result has been driven by William F Browne having the highest RPR compared to the other runners in this larger 16-horse field, but an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated in these weights. Large odds are on offer, and he clearly isn't fancied in the early market. Won early in his career but hasn't got much form to show since, hence the big price. The difference this time is cheekpieces are added to aid concentration, and a favorable draw in stall 4 can help. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Has shown ability in three of her starts and looked as though the run was needed two starts ago at Bellewstown over 8f. But was a major disappointment at Ballinrobe next time when upped in trip and in first-time blinkers. Made her handicap debut back on the AW last time and was a respectable 6th over 7f. Up to a mile now from the same mark and can reward each-way support in a first-time blinkers and tongue-tie combination.

Produced a dismal effort over hurdles on her first start for this stable but had shown much more promise in a maiden at Navan in April. She was drawn wide that day, a little keen which cost her late on over 10f. That maiden has worked out well, looking strong form. She makes her handicap debut back down in trip and on soft ground again, so might not be a completely forlorn hope.

Some Pretender is a 5-year-old daughter of Great Pretender ex Belle Brook, thus a half-sister to Mortlach by Yeats. She makes her racecourse debut here in this mares' bumper, where she'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father, W.P. Mullins. She's one for your horse tracker. The stable won this race last season with Cameletta Vega at 8/11f.

Action is a 2-year-old son of Frankel ex Gossamer Wings and thus a half-brother to Lambourn by Australia. Last time out on his racecourse debut, he was a 1-length third at 13/2 behind two stablemates, New Zealand 10/11f by Frankel and Isaac Newton 11/1 by Camelot. He'll now be ridden by W Lordan for Aidan O'Brien and Coolmore. He's drawn 4/10, and if he jumps and makes the rail position, he could make all and break his maiden tag. The stable won this 1m maiden last season with Puppet Master 1/2f by Camelot.
